---
title: "Performance & Reliability"
---

IrisPipe's correctness and reliability are validated through a **k6 integration test suite**
that runs against a real Spring Boot instance on every push to `main`.

[![k6 Regression](https://github.com/tibame201020/IrisPipe/actions/workflows/backend-k6.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/tibame201020/IrisPipe/actions/workflows/backend-k6.yml)

---

## Test Strategy

k6 is used for **integration-level correctness**, not synthetic load generation.
Each test suite:

1. Boots the real Spring Boot backend (from a compiled jar)
2. Runs a sequence of API calls that exercise a specific behavioral domain
3. Asserts on status codes, response shape, and state transitions
4. Tears down cleanly

This gives stronger coverage guarantees than unit tests for runtime semantics
because it exercises the full call stack: controller → service → Spring Batch → H2.

## CI Pipeline

The k6 suites run in **parallel matrix** on every PR and push to `main`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/backend-k6.yml (simplified)
strategy:
  matrix:
    suite: [config, workspace, pipeline-core, pipeline-resume,
            pipeline-stop, pipeline-operator-safety,
            pipeline-observability, pipeline-rerun,
            pipeline-control-loop, runtime]
```

Each matrix job:

1. Downloads the pre-built backend jar (shared artifact from `build-backend` job)
2. Starts the backend
3. Waits for health readiness (`/api/v1/sync-config` returns 200)
4. Runs the k6 suite with a namespaced prefix to avoid cross-suite state pollution
5. Uploads the backend log as artifact on failure

## Benchmark

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
results = FileAttachment("performance-results.json").json()

benchmark = results.benchmark
hasBenchmark = benchmark.execute_latency_p50_ms !== null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
hasBenchmark
  ? html`
    <table class="perf-table table table-sm">
      <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Execute latency p50</td><td>${benchmark.execute_latency_p50_ms} ms</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Execute latency p95</td><td>${benchmark.execute_latency_p95_ms} ms</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Execute latency p99</td><td>${benchmark.execute_latency_p99_ms} ms</td></tr>
        <tr><td>API latency p50</td><td>${benchmark.api_latency_p50_ms} ms</td></tr>
        <tr><td>API latency p95</td><td>${benchmark.api_latency_p95_ms} ms</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Throughput</td><td>${benchmark.throughput_rps} req/s</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>`
  : html`<p style="color:#9ca3af;font-style:italic;">
      Benchmark results not yet available.
      Run the <a href="https://github.com/tibame201020/IrisPipe/actions/workflows/k6-benchmark.yml">k6-benchmark workflow</a>
      to populate this section.
    </p>`
```

## Benchmark Methodology

The benchmark workflow (`k6-benchmark.yml`, runs on workflow dispatch or weekly schedule):

1. Builds the backend jar
2. Starts the backend with a clean H2 database
3. Runs a k6 script (`backend/k6/benchmark.js`) that:
   - Seeds a multi-stage pipeline definition
   - Executes the pipeline N times, measuring end-to-end latency
   - Measures API response times (`/api/v1/sync-config`, `/api/v1/sync-pipeline`)
   - Calculates throughput (requests/second under concurrency)
4. Parses k6 JSON output and updates `quarto/performance-results.json`
5. Commits the updated results file
6. Triggers a Quarto site rebuild and redeploy

This keeps the performance data live without requiring the backend to be hosted.
